rationale: I shot the town at seed 42, day 3, 10.4h and then MEASURED the shots rather than looking at them, because the last two bets that worked (#125's slate, #130's roofline) both came from a number and the ones that fizzled came from an impression. Classifying every canvas pixel back through project() into its ground class gives, as sd/mean over the class and share of a 1600x950 frame: ROAD 0.065 / 7.7%, GRASS 0.131 / 10.9%, PATH.court 0.143 / 9.3%, WATER 0.151 / 4.8%, SIDE.cross 0.185 / 4.1%, SIDE.quay 0.229 / 2.3%, WALL 0.240 / 12.3%. The roadway is three times flatter than the paving it runs beside, it is 7.7% of the frame, and it is the nearest big surface to the viewer — the one place LAWS says contrast should be HIGHEST. It is flat by construction and I found the two lines: groundBase's ROAD branch is the only ground colour whose hash term is halved (hv*0.5) over a pair six luma apart, and drawGround's ROAD branch strokes its setts at alpha .14 with off=(y%2)*0.5, so the bond alternates by row and never runs. That is #125's argument exactly — the biggest flat object in the picture, one iteration after the roof that held the title — and retiring a surface and laying it properly is rung 6 by name. The ladder did not force this climb (history 5, 6, 4b) and no signal is firing; the measurement forced it. The other four go to the four longest-untouched domains with every premise re-priced on HEAD by me, not by the cue that raised it: the quay really has no moorings and no hull ever ties there while the ticker has been saying 'a barge horn sounds somewhere far downstream' as one of its deliberately unplaced SOUNDS (b136, and it moves `structures`); LAWN_CAP is genuinely the only population cap whose knee has ever been swept, and the wide shot holds 42 people (b137); the plot lattice at ox 80..90 step 5 x oy 8..50 step 7 leaves a 1-cell way round every plot and there is not one shed, butt, cane or cloche on any of them (b138); and c205's 1.53 of GARDEN_ROWS 5 is #129's own measurement, so b139 arrives pre-counted and should be cheap.
